title: Famous games, annotated
summary: Eight celebrated games in the order they were played. In each you predict the key moves before seeing them, then see which core idea decided the game. The moves are facts checked against two sources; the commentary is original, and engine statements are marked as evidence at a stated depth.
audience: Anyone who has finished the first tactics and strategy lessons

title: History and the modern game
summary: How the rules, ratings, clocks and engines came to be. Historical claims are marked as secondary sources and are not machine-checked: the lessons say where they looked and where sources disagree.
audience: Anyone curious about where the game comes from

title: Opening deep dives
summary: Eighteen openings, one plan at a time: what the structures are, the plans for both sides, and what top-level games show. Every statement is a checked move order, an engine check at a stated depth, or one of our own statistics with its sample size.
audience: Anyone who has finished the opening principles lesson

title: Playstyles, measured
summary: What the games of named players measurably show, and what they cannot show. Every number comes from our own game data with its sample size; nothing is called a style unless a stated measure defines it.
audience: Anyone curious about how top players differ, and how to read statistics about people honestly

title: Stage checks
summary: One mixed, unlabelled check for each stage of the recommended path. Nothing is named and nothing is taught: you meet the positions cold, including positions where the right choice is a quiet move or to decline a tactic, and see afterwards what you could do without help.
audience: Anyone who has finished the lessons of a stage and wants to see what they can do unprompted
